No written contingency plan was available at the time of inspection. Per the registrant, they have no records or paperwork
retained and/or maintained. The contingency plan is to provide for the humane handling, treatment, transportation,
housing, and care of their animals in the event of an emergency or disaster. Not having a contingency plan doesn't ensure
the registrant will be prepared should an emergency or disaster occur. A written plan shall be developed and maintained
to provide guidance for the appropriate care of the animals during emergencies that could reasonably be anticipated. The
plan shall address specific tasks required to be carried out in response to the identified emergencies, personnel
responsible for the actions to be taken, chain of command, etc., as required in Section 2.134 of the Animal Welfare
regulations.
Correct by: November 15, 2026.

A goat escaped while in transport, when it was not placed into a primary enclosure or facility meeting the standard, after it
was removed from the transport vehicle, per the registrant. The goat was accepted for transportation from Columbia, MO
on January 26, 2026, for transport by the registrant. The next morning on January 27, 2026, in or near Mascoutah, IL ,
when cleaning the transport vehicle, the transporter removed the goat from the vehicle and leashed it. The transporter
closed the vehicle door on the leash to secure the goat to the vehicle. Per the registrant, the goat pulled back on the
leash, and the leash slipped through the closed door resulting in the goat’s escape. The animal was not recovered by the
registrant but instead found by a local farmer who recovered the goat for its owner. By not being held in a suitable
enclosure, the animal escaped which can result in stress, injury, exposure to diseases or death. Live animals shall not be
removed from their primary enclosures unless placed in other primary enclosures or facilities conforming to the
requirements in the Animal Welfare Act standards.
Correct by: October 31, 2026.
Per the registrant, they are no longer transporting and plan to cancel their registration. At the time of the delivery of this
report, there is no confirmation of cancellation.
The inspection was conducted with the registrant. An exit interview was offered, but the registrant did not respond to
multiple communication efforts.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
